headlines: NEW STUDY FINDS MIAMI BEACH TOWERS SINKING FROM ONGOING CONSTRUCTION
MIAMI BEACH SKYSCRAPERS ARE SINKING
WHY ARE COASTAL TOWERS IN SUNNY ISLES SLOWLY SINKING
draft.article: Continuous high-rise development across our barrier island is causing local towers to sink at varying speeds. A study by University of Miami professors Farzaneh Aziz Zanjani and Falk Amelung tracked 35 area buildings using satellite radar. While some waterfront properties sank roughly two centimeters between 2016 and 2023, towers in Surfside and Sunny Isles Beach dropped over eight centimeters. Impacted properties include the 60-story Porsche Design Tower, Trump Tower III, and the 87 Park tower. Researchers attribute the sinking to heavy loads and construction vibrations shifting the limestone and sand layers beneath our coastline, warning the movement is not expected to stop.

headlines: ONE DEAD AND TWO INJURED IN BISCAYNE BAY HELICOPTER CRASH
FATAL HELICOPTER CRASH IN BISCAYNE BAY
TRAGEDY ON BISCAYNE BAY DURING MIDDAY BOAT PHOTO FLIGHT
draft.article: Tragedy struck Biscayne Bay on Wednesday morning when a chartered photography helicopter crashed into the water east of Miami Executive Airport. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, the U.S. Coast Guard, and Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations rushed to the area following a mayday call around 11:15 a.m. Three people were aboard the Robinson R44, which was filming boats before going down. Rescuers discovered a good Samaritan attempting life-saving measures on one man, who died at the scene. Two other men were pulled from the water and taken to a hospital in critical but stable condition. Authorities report the cause of the crash remains under investigation.

headlines: MIAMI BEACH CONSIDERS HORSEBACK POLICE PATROLS BY 2028
MOUNTED POLICE PATROLS COULD RETURN TO MIAMI BEACH
WILL HORSES PATROL OCEAN DRIVE AGAIN AFTER DECADES AWAY?
draft.article: Miami Beach Mayor Steven Meiner and the city police chief are proposing the return of a mounted police unit by 2028 to boost crowd control on busy strips like Ocean Drive. The initial $500,000 cost would rely on private donations, keeping the first year free for taxpayers. Similar units currently patrol Coral Gables, the City of Miami, and Miami-Dade County. Commissioner David Suarez opposes the plan, calling it an expensive vanity project. Suarez raised issues regarding street cleanliness and horse welfare in South Florida heat and humidity. Horses previously patrolled Miami Beach during the 1930s and again through the 1980s and early 1990s.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE APPROVES 14.3 BILLION DOLLAR BUDGET FOR 2026-27
SPENDING TAX DOLLARS IS NOT THE SAME AS DELIVERING
CAN MIAMI-DADE BECOME THE BEST RUN COUNTY IN AMERICA
draft.article:
Miami-Dade County has locked in an approved budget of about $14.3 billion for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Now, local taxpayers want to see proof of what those public dollars actually buy.

County operations are directed by the mayor, while thirteen county commissioners hold responsibility for approving budgets and policy oversight. But accountability cannot stop after votes pass. Calls are growing for a public scoreboard tracking department performance, including road project costs, construction delays, contract delivery, and customer service response times.

Spending taxpayer funds is not the same as completing the work. To rank among the best-run counties in America, leaders must measure performance and report honest results.

The Miami Heat secured a thrilling 117-116 overtime road victory against the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday night at Intuit Dome.

The gritty road triumph brings Miami to 1-1 on its six-game West Coast swing and 3-5 on the season. Miami returns to action Thursday night against the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco.
